text:
Will Cuylle has 83 hits in 22 games, which tells you how he plays, and 8.1 expected goals of chances, which tells you he's more than a hitter. Only six of those chances have gone in, so our numbers list him as due. The Rangers' 24-year-old winger had the night to prove the point on Nov. 16, scoring twice against Montreal.

He's in the middle of the lineup and moving up: his ice time is up almost two minutes a night over the last ten games, to about 17 and a half. The Rangers get about 53% of the expected goals with him on at five on five, roughly what they manage without him, so he's holding his own rather than driving the line.

The defensive side is where he earned his spot last season. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 94th percentile among forwards at taking chances away, with most of his value from even-strength defense. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking adds that he gets the good passes, across the slot or from behind the net, but rarely carries the puck in himself. Watch the scoring. A player who keeps getting those looks usually catches up.
